study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Jalbrzikowski et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2019
study_identification_part.si4_title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Construct normative growth charts of amygdala functional connectivity in typically developing youths, quantify age-associated deviations in youths with psychosis spectrum disorders, and examine associations with psychotic symptoms.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The manuscript clearly describes four samples used for the study: three from University of Pittsburgh (Luna 1, Luna 2, and Pitt cohort) and one from University of Pennsylvania (Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort). These are explicitly named in Table 1 and described in the Methods section.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The final neuroimaging data set consisted of 1,062 participants 10-25 years old (typically developing control subjects, N=622; individuals with psychosis spectrum disorders, N=194; individuals with other psychopathology, N=246) from four different samples. Three data sets were acquired at the University of Pittsburgh and one at the University of Pennsylvania... The Luna 1, Luna 2, and Pitt cohorts were from the University of Pittsburgh, and the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort was from the University of Pennsylvania.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Youths with psychosis spectrum disorders lack normative age-related decreases in centromedial amygdala connectivity with prefrontal cortex, striatum, thalamus, and occipital cortex; greater deviation from normative CM amygdala–thalamus development relates to more severe positive symptoms.
